description: Search and maintain workspace-scoped long-term memory. A new remember proposal does not require a preliminary search; Runtime skips an already-active exact fact at commit. Search first only when revising or forgetting an existing memory. Store one short, self-contained sentence per memory, at most 120 characters. When several independent durable facts were established, issue several remember calls together in the same response so each gets its own category, vector, evidence, and lifecycle; a turn may stage at most eight changes. Never combine a paragraph or list into one memory, but keep conditions together when separating them would make a fact inaccurate. Remember only durable user preferences, project conventions, verified architecture, explicit decisions, or stable environment facts that will help future tasks. Never store secrets, guesses, transient task state, raw tool output, or facts useful only in the current turn. revise keeps the old record as superseded; forget expires a record without deleting its audit history.

propertyDescriptions.action: search retrieves existing memories; remember proposes one deduplicated atomic fact; revise supersedes; forget expires; recall reads captured historical tool evidence in the current thread without rerunning the tool.
propertyDescriptions.query: For search, use a concise keyword query or a memory ID.
propertyDescriptions.scope: For search, long_term (default) returns durable facts; history returns short current-thread evidence previews. Use recall on a preview ID for the captured text.
propertyDescriptions.limit: For search, 1-20 memory results. For recall, 1-16000 characters per evidence page (default 8000).
propertyDescriptions.evidenceId: For recall, use an evidence_ or context_ ID from a result/history preview, an ev_ ID from the compaction catalogue, or journal_message_<index> from the retired Journal range. All reads are restricted to the current thread. These references are evidence locators, not proofs of claims.
propertyDescriptions.offset: For recall, zero-based character offset; use nextOffset from the preceding page to continue.
propertyDescriptions.sourceRefs: For remember/revise, cite 1-8 captured evidence IDs from read_file for versioned project facts, or user for an explicit durable user preference/convention. Runtime requires resolvable sources before committing; source presence is not proof of arbitrary claims. Other observations belong in task history.
propertyDescriptions.includeInactive: For search only. Include superseded and expired audit-history entries.
propertyDescriptions.memoryId: For revise and forget, use a memory ID returned by memory search.
propertyDescriptions.content: For remember and revise, provide one short, self-contained durable fact with no secrets, lists, or bundled claims.
propertyDescriptions.category: For remember, classify the durable fact; a revision may preserve or replace the existing classification.
propertyDescriptions.reason: For a memory change, briefly state the current-turn evidence or reason and omit secrets.

guidance:
manage_memory is the only way you may maintain automatic long-term memory. Evaluate durable-memory changes once near the end of completed work. New remember proposals do not need a preliminary search: when several independently useful facts were established, issue several remember tool calls together in one response (up to eight changes per turn), and Runtime will skip exact active duplicates at commit. Search first only to obtain the memory ID needed for revise or forget. Store memory as atomic facts: one short, self-contained sentence per remember call, at most 120 characters, never a paragraph, list, or bundle of loosely related claims. Do not split conditions that must stay together to remain accurate, and give every fact its own current-turn evidence. Remember only durable user preferences, project conventions, verified architecture, established decisions, and stable environment facts. Revise a memory when newer evidence replaces it, and forget it when verified evidence shows it is no longer valid; retired rows remain in the local audit history. Never store secrets, uncertain claims, one-off task details, raw conversation summaries, or information already represented accurately. In Plan mode, only explicit durable user preferences or conventions may be remembered; proposed plan details are not verified facts.
Long-term-memory maintenance is your automatic responsibility, not a user-editing interface. A user may state a lasting preference or correct a project fact, which is evidence you should evaluate, but never perform an arbitrary memory mutation merely because the user asks to add, edit, delete, or target a memory ID. The /memory commands remain read-only.
Before your final answer, evaluate once whether this completed turn established, changed, or invalidated any durable memory. If so, call manage_memory with the necessary batched changes, then provide the final answer on the next step. Do not start multi-round memory searches for new facts, and do not call it merely to restate an existing memory.
